panels.stated_ethnicity_quote: A 3-year-old Palestinian girl was referred with primary complains of persistent chronic diarrhea and hypoalbumenemia since one year of age.
panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a 3-year-old child showing a photosensitive, scaly, desquamating, hyperpigmented rash on the face, neck and extremities, the classic pellagra-like dermatitis of Hartnup disease. The article's primary disease is Hartnup disease and the rash is attributed to it (celiac disease coexisting does not explain a photosensitive eruption). Real human patient image, adequately lit, eyes de-identified with a black bar.
panels.attribution_text: Ciecierega et al. Severe persistent unremitting dermatitis, chronic diarrhea and hypoalbuminemia in a child; Hartnup disease in setting of celiac disease.. BMC pediatrics 2014. doi:10.1186/s12887-014-0311-6. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Initial Presentation: significant photosensitivity with severe scaly desquamating skin rash and hyperpigmentation involving the face, neck, lower and upper extremities.
in_text_mentions: A 3-year-old Palestinian girl was referred with primary complains of persistent chronic diarrhea and hypoalbumenemia since one year of age.
